2609.01337.title: LEAP: Likelihood Elicitation and Aggregation for LLM-based Probabilistic Forecasting
2609.01337.paper_summary: LLM-based forecasting systems have improved on real-world tasks such as financial markets and sports outcomes, largely through stronger search and tool use. Many systems still ask an LLM to read all collected evidence together and produce the final forecast. We call this design Monolithic Prediction. It can obscure how individual evidence items affect the result and collapse uncertainty across competing outcomes. We propose LEAP (Likelihood Elicitation and Aggregation for Probabilistic forecasting), which reorganizes how collected evidence is used in the prediction stage. LEAP examines each evidence item separately and elicits likelihood parameters that describe its implications for the target. An explicit prior and a deterministic probabilistic model then combine these likelihoods into a posterior distribution. This procedure supports continuous, single-choice, and multi-choice forecasts while preserving reproducible evidence contributions. We build a benchmark covering forecasting, information-seeking, and browsing tasks, and evaluate LEAP on our own agent loop and several agent CLI frameworks. Given the same evidence, LEAP improves most prediction and calibration metrics across models and remains stronger under controlled comparisons of prior access, inference budget, and aggregation.
2609.01337.paper_summary_zh: LLM 基礎的預測系統在金融市場和體育結果等現實世界任務上有所改善，主要是通過更強的搜索和工具使用。許多系統仍然要求 LLM 將所有收集的證據一起閱讀並產生最終預測。我們稱這種設計為單體預測（Monolithic Prediction）。這可能會掩蓋個別證據項如何影響結果，並在競爭結果之間壓縮不確定性。我們提出了 LEAP（Likelihood Elicitation and Aggregation for Probabilistic forecasting），它重新組織了在預測階段如何使用收集的證據。LEAP 分別檢查每個證據項並引出描述其對目標影響的可能性參數。然後，明確的先驗和確定性概率模型將這些可能性結合成後驗分佈。這一程序支持連續的單選和多選預測，同時保留可重複的證據貢獻。我們建立了一個涵蓋預測、信息尋求和瀏覽任務的基準，並在我們自己的代理循環和幾個代理 CLI 框架上評估 LEAP。在相同證據的情況下，LEAP 在各模型中改善了大多數預測和校準指標，並在先驗訪問、推理預算和聚合的受控比較中仍然表現更強。
